items.title: Common application
items.summary: A complete project application most funders can use as it is: the project, the need, the plan, the budget and who leads the work. About 30 minutes for an applicant who knows the project.

forms.title: Common application
forms.description: A complete project application most funders can use as it is: the project, the need behind it, the plan, the budget and who will lead the work.
forms.instructions: Thank you for applying. Answer in plain language, as you would explain your work to a neighbor. Short answers are fine: the word limits are a ceiling, not a target. You can save and come back at any time before you submit.

items.title: General operating support application
items.summary: Unrestricted support for an organization's whole mission. Asks about the work, last year's results and the year ahead, and uses documents organizations already have.

forms.title: General operating support application
forms.description: Unrestricted support for an organization's whole mission, not one project. Asks about the work, last year's results and the year ahead.
forms.instructions: General operating support funds your organization as a whole: salaries, rent, technology and the work itself. Tell us about the organization, not a single project. Use the documents you already have; we do not need anything written just for us.

projectTitle.title: What should we call this request?

mission.title: Your mission and what you do

yearAhead.title: Your plans for the coming year

options.help: For example, "2027 operating support".
A few results you are proud of. Numbers, stories or both.
Optional. Knowing your challenges helps us be a better partner; it never counts against you.
An audit, a review or your board-approved statements, whichever you have.
The person we should talk to about this request.

items.title: Small capacity-building grant application
items.summary: A short application for small grants that strengthen how an organization works: fundraising, technology, training, board development or planning.

forms.title: Small capacity-building grant application
forms.description: A short application for a small grant that strengthens how an organization works: fundraising, technology, training, planning and the like.
forms.instructions: Capacity-building grants help your organization work better: new systems, skills or plans that will last after the grant ends. This application is short on purpose. Tell us what you want to strengthen and how.

success.title: How you will know it worked

options.help: For example, "New donor database" or "Board training".
What gets in the way today, and what it costs your organization.
A consultant, a trainer or a vendor, if you plan to work with one.
A simple list is fine: what you will buy or pay for, and roughly what each costs.
The person we should talk to about this request.

items.title: Five-criterion rubric
items.summary: Need and fit, approach, capacity, budget and community impact, each scored 1 to 5 with guidance for every score, so reviewers score the same way.

criteria.label: Need and fit
criteria.description: Is the need clear, and does the project fit this opportunity?
criteria.guidance: 5: a clear, local need and a close fit. 3: the need is plausible and the fit is partial. 1: the need is unclear or outside what this opportunity funds.

criteria.label: Approach
criteria.description: Is the plan realistic and likely to work?
criteria.guidance: 5: concrete steps, a sensible timeline, built on what has worked. 3: a reasonable plan with gaps. 1: the activities do not lead to the results described.

criteria.label: Capacity
criteria.description: Can the organization do what it proposes?
criteria.guidance: 5: experienced people and the systems to deliver. 3: some experience, some risk. 1: no clear way to deliver. Small organizations are not scored down for being small.

criteria.label: Budget
criteria.description: Is the budget reasonable and tied to the plan?
criteria.guidance: 5: every cost follows from the plan and the amounts are realistic. 3: mostly reasonable, some questions. 1: the budget does not match the plan.

criteria.label: Community impact
criteria.description: Will the project make a real difference for the people it serves?
criteria.guidance: 5: meaningful change for people who need it most, shaped with them. 3: some benefit. 1: little lasting difference.

items.title: Interim report
items.summary: A short mid-grant check-in: progress so far, people served to date, any change of plan and spending to date. Written so grantees can say plans changed.

forms.title: Interim report
forms.description: A mid-grant check-in: progress so far, numbers to date, any change of plan and spending to date.
forms.instructions: This check-in helps us understand how the work is going and whether we can help. It is not a test. If plans have changed, say so: changes are normal, and we would rather hear early.

supportNeeded.title: Is there anything we can do to help?

options.help: What you have done since the grant started.
Leave it blank if counting people does not fit your work.
Optional: anything that shows the work.

items.title: Final report
items.summary: The end-of-grant report: results against the goals, people served, what was learned, how the money was spent and a question about how you could be a better funder.

forms.title: Final report
forms.description: The end-of-grant report: what was accomplished, results against the goals, what was learned and how the money was spent.
forms.instructions: Thank you for the work this grant supported. Tell us what happened, including what did not go to plan: what you learned is as useful to us as what you achieved. Your answers from the application and any interim report are a good starting point.

goals.title: How the results compare with your goals

feedback.title: How could we have been a better funder?

options.help: Leave it blank if counting people does not fit your work.
Optional: one person, family or place this work made a difference for. Share only what they agreed to share.
Your project budget with a column for what you actually spent.

items.title: Award letter email
items.summary: A warm award email with the amount, what happens next and a link to review and sign. Uses the merge fields the GMS fills in for every award.

emails.name: Award letter
emails.subject: Good news: {{funder.name}} is awarding {{award.amount}} for {{award.title}}
emails.body:
Hello {{recipient.name}},

We are delighted to tell you that {{funder.name}} is awarding **{{award.amount}}** for **{{award.title}}**.

Thank you for the care you put into your application. Our reviewers were moved by your work and by what you hope to achieve.

What happens next:

1. Review the award and its conditions.
2. Sign the grant agreement.
3. Once both sides have signed, we will schedule the first payment.

[Review the award and sign]({{links.award}})

If anything in the award is unclear, or the timing does not work for you, reply to this email. We would much rather sort it out now.

Congratulations, and thank you for the work you do.

{{funder.name}}

items.title: Decline email
items.summary: A kind, clear decline: thanks the applicant, says the decision is not a judgment of their work, keeps their application available and offers feedback.

emails.name: Decline
emails.subject: Your application to {{funder.name}}
emails.body:
Hello {{recipient.name}},

Thank you for applying to {{opportunity.title}} and for the time you gave to **{{application.title}}**.

We are sorry to tell you that {{funder.name}} is not able to fund it this time. We received many more strong applications than we could support, and this decision is not a judgment of the value of your work.

Your application stays in your records, so you can reuse what you wrote: [View your application]({{links.status}})

We hope you will apply again. If you would like feedback on your application, reply to this email and we will do our best to help.

With thanks and best wishes,

{{funder.name}}

items.title: Small grants program kit
items.summary: Everything to run a first grant round: the common application, the five-criterion rubric, the final report, and the award and decline emails. Copy it and adjust what you need.
